# Exact obstruction to the proposed six-sector product inequality

Let

    K=conv{(-19,-18),(19,-3),(-4,7)},
    H_1={x>=0}, H_2={y>=0}, H_3={x+y<=0}.

The normals (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) form a positive rank-two circuit.
The halfplanes cover the entire plane, and their boundaries meet at
the origin. The origin is interior to K: in its counterclockwise
vertex order, the oriented cross products of each edge with the
vector to zero are (399,121,205), all positive; the verifier below
computes these directly. Equivalently its strictly positive barycentric
coordinates are (121/725,205/725,399/725).

Write A_i=|K intersect H_i|, let T_i be the area captured by the two
caps other than i, and let S_i be the area captured only by cap i.
The triple intersection is one point, so S_i=A_i-sum_j T_j+T_i.
Direct rational polygon clipping gives

    |K|=725/2,
    A=(13775/92, 1421/20, 198505/848),
    T=(1681/80, 8379/212, 14641/460),
    S=(83079/1060, 6701/368, 3471/20).

Consequently

    product(S_i)/product(T_i)
       =214705407501/22913326051 > 8,
    product(S_i)-8 product(T_i)
       =282589191837/7801600 > 0.

Thus the proposed inequality product(S_i)<=8 product(T_i) is false
even for an actual rational triangle and a concurrent positive circuit.
It cannot supply a universal proof of the overlap-minimum theorem.
There is no conflict with that different inequality: here

    sum_i T_i/min_i A_i=310599/238924>1.

The companion verifier clips the actual triangle using Fraction
arithmetic and checks each printed value and strict sign. The example
was discovered by a numerical screen, but these exact geometric and
arithmetic certificates, not the screen, prove the obstruction.
